name: ponytail
description: Makes your AI agent think like the laziest senior dev in the room. The best code is the code you never wrote.
one_liner: A set of instructions that makes an AI coding assistant act like a grumpy, experienced senior developer — it reuses what's already in your code instead of writing hundreds of new lines for a simple feature.
buyer: An engineering lead at a startup who's watched their AI coding tool's token bill and codebase size balloon and wants both back under control.
business_use_cases: A startup's eng lead installs it team-wide to cut AI-written code volume and token spend without changing which AI tool they use.
A contract developer uses it on client projects to keep AI-generated pull requests small enough for a human to actually review.
A bootcamp teaching AI-assisted development uses it to show students the difference between lazy AI code and bloated AI code.

money_ideas.idea: No direct revenue model — it is a free skill/plugin, not a product; value capture would require bundling it into a paid consulting offer.

steal_this: There isn't a real business here to build on top of a free prompt-engineering skill; the closest honest play is a short paid workshop teaching teams 'how to prompt your AI agent to write less code,' using this as the lesson.
